findings.explanation: The query uses SQLAlchemy's ORM filter method with a bound parameter (Order.user_id == user_id), which prevents SQL injection.

The endpoint /<int:user_id>/orders allows any authenticated user to retrieve the orders of any other user by simply changing the user_id in the URL. There is no check to ensure the requesting user is the owner of the orders or an administrator, leading to an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR).
findings.suggested_fix: Add an authorization check to ensure the current user is either the owner of the orders (g.user.id == user_id) or has the appropriate role (e.g., admin) to view other users' orders. For example: if g.user.id != user_id and not is_owner_or_admin(g.user, user_id): abort(403).
